title: Filtered colimits of cocartesian fibrations and of operads on total categories
statement: Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Use the ordinary and generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. For a small infinity category $B$, let $\operatorname{coCart}(B)$ be the infinity category of small cocartesian fibrations over $B$ and functors over $B$ preserving cocartesian arrows, as in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. The total-category functor $\operatorname{coCart}(B)\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$, $(q:\mathcal E\to B)\mapsto\mathcal E$, preserves small filtered colimits: it carries every colimiting cocone of a small filtered diagram in $\operatorname{coCart}(B)$ to a colimiting cocone in $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$. The forgetful functor from ordinary nonsymmetric infinity operads to $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$, and the one from generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads, detect filtered colimits: a filtered cocone of operads is colimiting if and only if its underlying cocone of total infinity categories is colimiting. All assertions concern small filtered infinity categories and coherent diagrams, without restricting the transition functors to be fully faithful.

source.place: Corollaries 3.3.3–3.3.4 with Proposition 3.3.2 and Lemma 3.3.6 (forgetting the slice base) for the total-category functor; Theorem 3.3.1 for detection by the operadic forgetful functors. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text:
First work in the slice $\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty/B}$. The cone-mapping formula of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] with the one-point diagram of value $B$ identifies, for $p:E\to B$ and $q:T\to B$,
$$\operatorname{Map}_{/B}(p,q)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{p}\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cat}_\infty}(E,T)\xrightarrow{q\circ-}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cat}_\infty}(E,B)\bigr).$$
Here the slice is the coherent cone category on that one-point diagram, so this is exactly the cited formula, including triangle homotopies. For a small filtered diagram $p_i:E_i\to B$, form $E=\operatorname{colim}_iE_i$, whose existence is [lem-coef-cat-infinity-filtered-finite-calculus]. The coherent structural maps to $B$ induce $p:E\to B$ by the mapping-space colimit test of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. Applying the displayed fiber formula and that test twice gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{/B}(p,q)\simeq\lim_{i\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{/B}(p_i,q).$$
Indeed both ambient mapping spaces become limits and taking a fiber over the compatible structural maps commutes with that limit: both constructions specify the same families of points, paths and their coherences. Thus this is a colimit in the slice. Conversely, a colimit cocone in this slice is colimiting on total categories: test it on $T\times B\to B$ for arbitrary $T$. Finite products in $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ are the products of infinity categories by [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], so maps into this slice object are exactly maps to $T$; apply the same mapping-space test. This establishes the required equivalence of colimit cocones in the slice and on total categories.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.6, with the slice fiber calculation written out

proof.text: Keep such a filtered slice diagram, and select any collection $A$ of base arrows over which every $p_i$ has cocartesian lifts preserved by the transition functors. This includes $A$ all arrows of $B$, and later $A$ the inert arrows of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. We prove that every stage cocartesian lift over an arrow of $A$ remains cocartesian in $E$. Let $e:x\to y$ in $E_i$ be such a lift. For a testing object $z\in E$, the object-representation clause of [lem-coef-cat-infinity-filtered-finite-calculus] supplies $z_k\in E_k$ and an equivalence $r_kz_k\simeq z$. Filteredness supplies a stage $j$ and arrows $i\to j$, $k\to j$. Use the transition image of the original $e$ at $j$, which is cocartesian by hypothesis, and the transition image of $z_k$ as the testing object. This retains the specified lift; it does not select an arbitrary new representative of $e$. Equivalence of testing objects changes all mapping spaces by equivalences. At every later stage the square with top row $\operatorname{Map}(y,z)\to\operatorname{Map}(x,z)$ and bottom row $\operatorname{Map}_B(py,pz)\to\operatorname{Map}_B(px,pz)$ is a homotopy pullback, by the intrinsic cocartesian-arrow criterion in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. Equivalently, on the homotopy fiber over every $g:py\to pz$, the map $\operatorname{Map}^{g}(y,z)\to\operatorname{Map}^{g\,p(e)}(x,z)$ is an equivalence. The relative mapping-space formula and its precomposition naturality in [lem-coef-cat-infinity-filtered-finite-calculus] identify the same map in $E$ with the filtered colimit of these equivalences, so it is an equivalence for every $g$. Hence the square in $E$ is a homotopy pullback and $r_i(e)$ is cocartesian. To obtain a lift out of an arbitrary object of $E_b$, use the finite-limit comparison in that same node to identify $E_b\simeq\operatorname{colim}_i(E_i)_b$. Its object-representation clause supplies an object at a stage together with an equivalence in this fiber. Lift the given base arrow there and precompose with the inverse fiber equivalence. The mapping-square criterion is invariant under that precomposition because it changes its rows by equivalences. Thus $p$ has all the required lifts.

Every $p$-cocartesian arrow over $f\in A$ differs, up to a commuting triangle, from one of the lifts just constructed by an equivalence over the target identity. Here is the uniqueness argument from the criterion of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. For two cocartesian arrows $e:x\to y$, $e':x\to y'$ over $f$, taking the fiber of the mapping-square equivalence over $1_{py}$ or $1_{py'}$ gives arrows $a:y\to y'$ and $b:y'\to y$ over identities with $ae\simeq e'$ and $be'\simeq e$. Injectivity up to homotopy of those same equivalences gives $ba\simeq1_y$ and $ab\simeq1_{y'}$, including the triangle compatibilities. Thus $a$ is an equivalence. Changing the source by the fiber equivalence from step 2 changes no conclusion. Consequently a functor $H:E\to T$ over $B$ preserves cocartesian arrows over $A$ if and only if all $Hr_i$ do: the forward direction uses step 2, and for the reverse direction compare each arrow with a stage lift as above, then use that functors preserve equivalences and the mapping-square criterion is invariant under precomposition or postcomposition with an equivalence over an identity. The same assertion holds through every equivalence between such functors, so the subspace of preserving functors is a union of components of the slice mapping space. Restriction therefore identifies this subspace with the subspace of the limit in step 1 whose components at every stage preserve the selected lifts. This concerns entire mapping spaces: an $n$-simplex of a core consists of preserving vertex functors and equivalences between them, and restriction retains all its faces and higher compatibilities.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.2 (iii); uniqueness of cocartesian lifts expanded

proof.text:
Apply steps 1-3 with $A$ all arrows of $B$. The intrinsic-to-simplicial comparison in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] represents $p:E\to B$ by a cocartesian fibration with the same total infinity category. The cocartesian version of [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model] identifies its mapping Kan complex into another cocartesian fibration with the core of the full functor subcategory on cocartesian-preserving maps. Thus the restricted mapping-space equivalence from step 3 is
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{coCart}(B)}(E,T)\simeq\lim_{i\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{coCart}(B)}(E_i,T).$$
The colimit test of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] says this cocone is colimiting in $\operatorname{coCart}(B)$. Any other colimiting cocone is equivalent to it by its universal property; the equivalence and its inverse are cocartesian-preserving functors, so their underlying total functors are inverse equivalences. The underlying cocone is therefore the colimit cocone of total categories constructed in step 1. This proves preservation for every small filtered coherent diagram.

Now put $B=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ and let $E_i$ be ordinary or generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads. Their maps preserve the cocartesian lifts over inert arrows by the operad conventions in [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. Apply steps 1-3 with $A$ exactly those arrows. We may represent the resulting slice object $p:E\to B$ by an inner fibration: factor $p$ as a categorical trivial cofibration followed by a Joyal fibration using [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. The latter is an inner fibration because every inner horn inclusion is a trivial cofibration, as the same node states. Since $B$ is a quasicategory, the replacement total object is a quasicategory. This replacement changes the total category by an equivalence over $B$, so it preserves the intrinsic mapping-square calculations and the slice mapping spaces. The intrinsic cocartesian criterion from [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] supplies precisely the inert lifts in this representative. It remains to check the Segal and relative mapping-space axioms; we do so at every arity, without passing a limit over all arities through the filtered colimit.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.3.1, construction of the inert-lift slice colimit

proof.text:
For each $n$, the finite-limit clause of [lem-coef-cat-infinity-filtered-finite-calculus] gives $E_{[n]}\simeq\operatorname{colim}_i(E_i)_{[n]}$. In the ordinary case, the Segal comparisons at the stages and their inert-projection naturality give
$$E_{[n]}\simeq\operatorname{colim}_i((E_i)_{[1]}^n)\simeq(E_{[1]})^n.$$
For $n=0$ this uses the empty-limit clause, so $E_{[0]}$ is terminal. For generalized operads take instead the finite incidence diagram with one edge object for each consecutive pair in $[n]$, one vertex object for each vertex, and an arrow from an edge to each of its endpoints. Its limit is the iterated fiber product of the unary fibers over the zero-fiber. The stage Segal equivalences in [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability], the finite-limit comparison, and the same naturality identify $E_{[n]}$ with this limit of $E_{[1]}$ and $E_{[0]}$. When $n=0$ the incidence diagram is the single vertex, and the comparison is the identity of $E_{[0]}$. If zero-fibers are required to be spaces, this requirement is retained: every arrow in their filtered colimit is represented at a stage by the finite-data clause, where it is invertible; its inverse and inverse homotopies remain an inverse in the colimit. Thus all arrows of the colimit zero-fiber are equivalences. It equals its core, which is Kan by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], and hence is a space.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.3.1, Segal comparison, including arity zero

proof.text:
Fix $x\in E_{[m]}$, $y\in E_{[n]}$, and a base arrow $\phi:[m]\to[n]$. By the fiber-colimit comparisons of step 6 and the object-representation clause of [lem-coef-cat-infinity-filtered-finite-calculus], represent $x$ and $y$ by objects in the stage fibers over $[m]$ and $[n]$, with equivalences in those fibers. Filteredness moves these representatives to one stage. Choose there the finite coherent diagram of inert lifts out of the representative of $y$; at later stages use its transition image. The fiber equivalences identify the relative mapping-space tests for these representatives with those for $x,y$, while leaving the base arrow $\phi$ fixed. Their images are inert lifts in $E$ by step 2, and step 3 compares any other chosen inert lifts to these by equivalences. The ordinary operadic mapping axiom of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability] gives at every later stage
$$\operatorname{Map}^{\phi}(x,y)\simeq\prod_{a=1}^n\operatorname{Map}^{\rho_a\phi}(x,y_a).$$
The relative mapping-space and composition comparisons of [lem-coef-cat-infinity-filtered-finite-calculus] identify the map in $E$ with the colimit of these stage comparisons. By [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] with $\kappa=\aleph_0$, that colimit of finite products is the product of the colimits, including the empty product when $n=0$. Hence it is the required equivalence in $E$. For generalized operads, replace the discrete collection of unary projections by the finite incidence category of inert maps $\alpha:[n]\to[1]$ and $[n]\to[0]$ and their endpoint factorizations. The relative limit axiom is
$$\operatorname{Map}^{\phi}(x,y)\simeq\lim_{\alpha}\operatorname{Map}^{\alpha\phi}(x,y_\alpha).$$
The incidence category has no nonidentity composable pair, so its nerve has finitely many nondegenerate simplices. Apply exactly the same relative mapping-space comparison and the finite-limit assertion for spaces to this finite nerve. All maps are postcomposition with the chosen inert lifts, and the naturality clause in the finite-data node identifies them with the stage maps. This proves the generalized mapping axiom, including the single-vertex diagram for $n=0$. Together with steps 5-6, $E$ is an operad of the required kind.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.3.1, relative mapping-space decomposition and generalized finite incidence diagrams

proof.text:
For an operad $P$ the mapping-space identification in [lem-coef-marked-operadic-model-structures] identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Opd}}(E,P)$ with the core of the full category of inert-preserving functors over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. Steps 1 and 3 therefore restrict to the equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Opd}}(E,P)\simeq\lim_{i\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Opd}}(E_i,P).$$
By [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] the cocone with vertex $E$ is an operadic colimit. This proves preservation by the forgetful functor, since its underlying cocone was constructed as a colimit. It also proves reflection: for any operadic cocone with vertex $Q$ whose total cocone is colimiting, the operadic colimit property just proved induces an inert-preserving comparison $E\to Q$, and the underlying universal properties make it an equivalence of total categories. An inverse equivalence over the base preserves inert arrows, since an equivalence over the base identifies the mapping-space squares characterizing cocartesian arrows in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. Thus it is an equivalence of operads; the cocone with vertex $Q$ is colimiting as well. Conversely every operadic colimit cocone is equivalent to the constructed one, so is colimiting on total categories. The argument uses coherent diagrams and mapping-space universal properties throughout; it never assumes ordinary indexing categories or fully faithful transitions.

split_report.summary: Expanded the source Section 3.3 argument into eight steps. One new statement-only finite-data theorem for filtered colimits in Cat infinity; no clause-restating cocartesian or operadic node. Proved slice creation through mapping fibers; proved persistence, existence and uniqueness of cocartesian lifts; checked all ordinary and generalized Segal and mapping axioms, including nullary arity, and the preservation/reflection universal properties. Searched the entire DAG, blueprint and Lean source and ran logged Mathlib searches. Statement unchanged. Second reading specifies transition images of lifts and fiberwise representatives, and adds the explicit space-category definition to the new node.
